title: Connected generic fibre of a flat degeneration over a DVR
statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring and f:X→Spec R a flat morphism with X connected and nonempty. If the scheme-theoretic closed fibre is reduced, the scheme-theoretic fibre over the zero prime is connected and nonempty. No finiteness or separatedness assumption is imposed.

proof.text: Nonemptiness: choose x in X. The zero prime specializes to f(x). Mathlib Flat.generalizingMap lifts this generalization to y in X mapping to the zero prime. The fibre homeomorphism supplies a point in the generic fibre.

Injectivity on every open: the residue-field point at the zero prime has dense image in Spec R. Spec R is reduced, so this point map is scheme-theoretically dominant; it is quasi-compact since both schemes are affine. Scheme-theoretic dominance and quasi-compactness persist under flat base change. Mathlib Scheme.Hom.app_injective therefore gives injectivity of the generic fibre restriction on every open.

For every affine U, the canonical affine ring models supply reducedness of A/pi A and the generic localization isomorphism with its restriction equation. Flatness of R to A follows from f.flat_appLE composed with the spectrum global-section isomorphism. Apply the already proved algebraic extension theorem and transport its lift back through the ring isomorphism.

Given a global generic-fibre idempotent, choose these affine lifts. Naturality of the fibre section maps and composition of restrictions show their images agree on every overlap. Injectivity on those overlaps implies the lifts agree, so the structure-sheaf unique-gluing theorem gives a global section b on X. The inverse images of affine opens cover the generic fibre; the sheaf local-equality theorem proves i^*(b)=e.

Injectivity of the global restriction implies b squared equals b. Apply the already proved scheme idempotent criterion to the connected total space X: b=0 or b=1. Mapping this equality into the generic fibre gives e=0 or e=1. With its proved nonemptiness, the same criterion proves the generic fibre connected.

proof_origin.note: R3 formalized nonemptiness, restriction injectivity, the ring-level extension, overlap compatibility, sheaf gluing and the idempotent criterion. Only canonical affine fibre ring models remain as a new named theorem.
